correctness.rationale: The exact fixed-gap Gram matrix is positive definite and yields K_d(x)=2(1-s cos(dx))/(1-s²). For d>=2 the absolute sinc bound makes K<4. For 0<d<2, alternating-sine estimates yield q0<=1-s<=u/6, u=d²<4; F_u(q)=2q(3-2q)-(1-q)u strictly increases on the allowed interval and F_u(q0)=u²(20+10u-u²)/3600>0. This forces K<1+3x² for every |x|>=1. A cos(ht)+3x sin(ht)/h witness tends to the affine polynomial 1+3xt, whose evaluation ratio equals 1+3x²; every fixed positive gap is strictly below, proving nonattainment. The single-frequency case has ratio 1. Exact symbolic identities were verified by the embedded script, numerical checks are supplementary and not relied on as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Zhang 2026 makes exterior sparse-Fourier leverage a natural quantitative invariant for prediction outside sampled intervals but gives only scale-level bounds. The exact k=2 profile 1+3x² solves the first nontrivial unseparated real-frequency case and identifies the decisive frequency-collision extremal mechanism and nonattainment. This is a substantive sharp bound throughout an unbounded continuum of exterior points, not a numerical sample or arbitrary parameter tweak. The restriction to exterior points is mathematically genuine, with a constructed interior counterexample.
